races.name: Nxt Big Thing Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Kingmoor Park Properties Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Peace Belle
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with a win on Good going and the highest OR in the field at 120; 39 days off is not a concern for a five-year-old with placed form at this trip, but she will need Aleatrix to set a pace strong enough to reel in from the rear.

runners_data.name: Aleatrix
runners_data.note: The race-shaper: sole front-runner, two runs both on Good going producing a win and a second, and stepping up to 1m3f for the first time — stamina over the extra distance is the key query, but Ralph Beckett's fillies often stay well and her tactical control here is a significant asset.

runners_data.name: Green Area
runners_data.note: Consistent but winless, with back-to-back thirds on Good ground at 10f and 12f; Charlie Johnston's runner has form over 12f and steps up to 13f, and while she stays, she needs Aleatrix to tire to get competitive from her hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Lazy In Red
runners_data.note: Unraced or debutant with no form string and going tagged UNKNOWN — Donald Whillans sends her out with a single 14-day entry, making her impossible to assess tactically; the weight of ignorance argues against her, but any hidden ability on debut could create chaos at the front.

races.paceDynamic: Aleatrix is the sole confirmed front-runner in a four-runner field and will lead from the outset at Carlisle's 1m3f trip, almost certainly unopposed through the early stages given that Peace Belle, Green Area, and the unknown Lazy In Red are all mapped as hold-up or unclassified types. With no rival willing or able to challenge her for the lead, Aleatrix can control tempo entirely on her own terms, setting a pace that is manageable rather than pressured — a crucial advantage over a stamina-testing distance on Good ground. The race is therefore likely to be run at a measured, even gallop until the final turn, where Aleatrix can choose her own moment to quicken. This shape strongly favours Aleatrix's front-running profile and makes life harder for the hold-up horses, who will need a genuine test of stamina in the closing stages to reel in a front-runner who has conserved energy throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Aleatrix Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Aleatrix leads cleanly and controls tempo throughout, denying the hold-up horses enough pace to close.
scenarios.body: Aleatrix settles into an uncontested rhythm, conserving energy through the middle stages before kicking clear entering the straight; with no rival having dictated the pace against her, she has the reserves to repel any late challenges. This scenario suits a front-runner who has already won and placed on Good ground and whose jockey Paul Mulrennan is well capable of judging a solo lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough in the final quarter-mile to stop Aleatrix, allowing the closers to catch her.
scenarios.body: Peace Belle, the highest-rated runner on OR=120 with a course-applicable win on Good ground, is best placed among the closers to launch a late challenge if stamina becomes decisive over 1m3f. Green Area, also rated 120 and consistently placed on Good going, could join the finish if the fractions are honest enough to string out the field.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lazy In Red Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If the unknown Lazy In Red shows natural early pace and makes this a true test, unsettling Aleatrix's rhythm.
scenarios.body: With no form on record and going tagged UNKNOWN, Lazy In Red is a wildcard who could emerge as an unexpected pace factor if she proves to have natural speed — disrupting Aleatrix's controlled lead and forcing a faster early gallop. If the tempo rises, stamina-laden closers benefit but Lazy In Red herself could be exposed before the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Aleatrix sets an overly conservative tempo, allowing all rivals to coast into contention before a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A dawdle would theoretically compress the field and turn 1m3f into a short-distance test, but with four runners and an experienced pilot in Mulrennan, a truly crawling pace is unlikely — and none of the hold-up horses are proven sprinters. The scenario exists on paper but carries minimal weight given the configuration.

watchPoints.text: Aleatrix — watch how Mulrennan manages the early tempo; if she bowls along freely rather than dawdling, this race is effectively over from halfway and no hold-up horse is likely to close.
Peace Belle — if Andrew Mullen positions her closer than her usual hold-up tag suggests in a four-runner field, she becomes a far more dangerous finisher over 1m3f.
Lazy In Red — a complete unknown on debut; if she breaks fast and pushes Aleatrix into a pace battle, the entire race shape changes and closers benefit substantially.
Green Area — 54 days between runs is the longest gap in the field; if she needs the run after that layoff, her chance of closing the gap on Aleatrix in the straight is significantly diminished.

races.name: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Fate's Gambit
runners_data.note: Placed third in similar Going on the all-weather but form figures of 355093 over 6-8f show no win; Ruth Carr has a fair 14-day strike rate and James Sullivan is capable, but this horse is a natural hold-up type thrust onto the lead by default — style fitness is the central risk if rivals apply any pressure in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Fate's Gambit shaped with clear promise when third last time out, and he returns 26 days later fit and fresh, carrying 133 lb from stall 8 over a trip he has run over before; yet to win in recent starts, but our rating of 70 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Zous Juice
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby runner returning after 60 days off with a form string of 94-90 suggesting consistency at midfield-to-rear; a true hold-up horse competing over a shorter 7f than its recent 8f outings, and on Good ground where its 0W0P record from six similar-going runs is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Zous Juice nevertheless catches the eye with experience over today's trip and going, and a rating of 63 that suggests he retains more ability than his official mark of 54 implies; the 60-day absence, however, is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Blairtum Night
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt handler with a modest 14-day record; the 4/8f Good ground run last time is its best recent effort, but at 7f on this course the horse naturally wants to come late — with so many others also wanting to do the same, a clear run from the rear is far from guaranteed.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Blairtum Night makes little appeal, though he has run over today's trip before and 34 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Why Because
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley runner with David Nolan up, wearing a hood; 19 days since last run and a consistent if winless record at 7f on Good, with three placed efforts from eight similar-going outings — travels prominently and is one of the few in this field genuinely able to race in or near its natural position.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of the ten runners on our figures, Why Because has experience of today's distance and going and comes here nicely fresh at 19 days since her last outing, carrying 138 lb from stall one; the concern is that she has been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Renewable Dream
runners_data.note: John Wainwright's runner has placed twice from 10 similar-going starts; Gianluca Sanna claims 5lb which is significant at this level, and the 32-day break looks manageable — sits as one of the genuine prominent types able to race close to Fate's Gambit, making it structurally well-placed in this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Renewable Dream shaped with promise when third five starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going with 32 days between runs suggesting he arrives fresh; the risk is a winless run of recent form that includes several mid-field finishes.

runners_data.name: Reenie's Dream
runners_data.note: Bryan Smart runner off a big 113-day absence, which is the longest layoff in the field and a notable flag; all five recent runs came on Standard ground at AW tracks and this Good turf is an unknown surface variable — its true hold-up style means it is unlikely to secure the midfield position shown on the map.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 113 days, Reenie's Dream does have experience of today's trip and going in her favour, though a fourth two starts back is the best she can offer from recent outings, and she faces a stiff task from a midfield draw carrying 133 lb.

runners_data.name: April Diamond
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine sends this 5-year-old 19 days after last run; the 2/6f Good ground effort is its best recent form, and Andrew Mullen takes the ride — a natural hold-up horse with limited scope to get closer than its natural rear-of-field position given the traffic ahead of it.
runners_data.comment: April Diamond has experience over today's trip and going, and returns fit after 19 days, but she is winless in her last six starts, with her best recent effort a second three starts back and a sixth last time out — a mid-division profile that makes her difficult to fancy off 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Rajawail
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Brian Rothwell wearing a tongue strap, back just 8 days after its last start over 8-12f trips — the drop to 7f is a significant distance compression and its 0W0P record from 13 similar-going starts is the weakest in the field; racing out of role at the rear makes a big impact unlikely.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Rajawail faces a stiff ask, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a sharp eight-day turnaround carrying 124 lb from stall two.

runners_data.name: Long Shot
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has an excellent 14-day strike rate (5 from 84) and Long Shot wears a hood; three placings from 12 similar-going starts show some form, and Oisin McSweeney is a competent conditional — at 7f its 4/7f Good run is encouraging, and if any pace develops it has the profile to close.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Long Shot nevertheless shows consistency at this level with a pair of seconds in recent form, and has run over today's trip and going before; the 121 lb burden and ranking of seventh of ten suggest he faces a stiff task, though 19 days off should leave him fresh.

runners_data.name: Runninman
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans runner with a 1/1 14-day record, wearing a hood; form of 368740 on Standard surfaces with no similar-going wins in 12 attempts makes this a significant query on Good turf — a 3-year-old facing elders, and its natural hold-up style means it needs a strong pace it is unlikely to get in this race.
runners_data.comment: Runninman has been winless in his last six starts, with just a third among a string of modest efforts and an unplaced run most recently, and ranked ninth of ten on our figures he faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a manageable 19-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Fate's Gambit is the sole confirmed pace-setter in this 10-runner field, redistributed to the lead as the most likely pace-maker, and on Good ground over 7f at Carlisle is expected to control proceedings at a sustainable, uncontested tempo — nothing here will seriously pressurise them early. The bulk of the field are genuine hold-up or midfield types, meaning the race will likely shape as a single-file procession through the early and middle stages before the tempo lifts in the straight. With no rivals pressing Fate's Gambit, the pace will be honest but not extreme, creating a steady gallop that compresses the field and reduces the premium on finishing speed from far back. This shape most favours runners able to travel prominently or at least in the first half of the field, as the lack of genuine early pace injection means pure closers will find ground hard to make up from deep; horses that can sit within two or three lengths of the leader and produce a sustained run are best placed. This field holds significantly more hold-up and rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate — Reenie's Dream, Zous Juice, Blairtum Night, April Diamond, Rajawail, Long Shot and Runninman are all natural hold-up horses pushed forward on the map; in practice, most will not secure a position any closer than midfield, with Why Because and Renewable Dream the most likely to travel prominently behind Fate's Gambit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fate's Gambit Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fate's Gambit bowls along at a comfortable solo gallop and the chasing pack fail to close the gap until too late.
scenarios.body: Fate's Gambit dictates a moderate tempo on Good ground with no rival willing to go with them, meaning any meaningful kick comes only inside the final 2f when ground has been covered comfortably; the light weight of opposition pace means the leader preserves enough energy to hold on. Runners who can track closely — Why Because and Renewable Dream — are best placed to pounce if the leader does tire, but a genuine pace advantage with no pressure is a serious positive for Fate's Gambit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Fate's Gambit sets a pace that proves just strong enough to string the field out, and the closet pursuers time their run to hit the front inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Why Because, tracked by Renewable Dream, sits within two lengths of the pace throughout and produces the most sustained gallop in the straight to collar Fate's Gambit close home; the Good ground and 7f trip at Carlisle suits a horse travelling with cover before producing a clean, straight-line challenge. This scenario rewards the one or two horses who genuinely get to race in their natural position rather than being squeezed wide or too deep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fate's Gambit goes quicker than expected through the middle sections, setting up a truly run race that burns off the prominent types and leaves the late finishers with a real target.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated pace would open a window for the genuine hold-up horses — Long Shot and April Diamond — to pick off tiring rivals in the final furlong, though both are operating slightly out of their natural position in this map and face a compressed draw with little pace injection. This is the least structurally likely outcome given the absence of pace pressure on Fate's Gambit, making a truly searching gallop improbable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Fate's Gambit is checked or eased mid-race, causing the entire field to bunch and produce a chaotic sprint finish up the Carlisle straight.
scenarios.body: The lack of any secondary pace source means a check or tactical disruption would concertina the entire field into a tight group from the 3f pole, making the outcome highly unpredictable and reducing the advantage of any specific running style. In this scenario, a horse with a sharp turn of foot and a clear run — potentially Renewable Dream or Long Shot — could benefit from the resulting gaps.

watchPoints.text: Fate's Gambit leads by default despite being a natural hold-up type — watch whether James Sullivan controls the fractions or allows the gallop to drift too slow, as that directly determines whether any hold-up horse can land a blow.

Renewable Dream's 5lb claim for Gianluca Sanna is the biggest weight pull in the race — if it travels smoothly just off Fate's Gambit's shoulder, it could prove a decisive edge in a closely-matched maiden handicap field.

Reenie's Dream has not run for 113 days and all its form is on Standard AW — monitor its behaviour in the pre-parade ring and whether it handles the Good turf, as it could be an unfancied drifter if connections are using this as a pipe-opener.

Long Shot's trainer Tim Easterby is striking at 5 from 84 runners in the last 14 days — a stat worth noting even if the horse is unlikely to race in the prominent position it needs to take maximum advantage of the race shape.

The combination of Rajawail running just 8 days after its last start and stepping sharply down in trip from 8-12f to 7f is a flag for pace-watchers — if the horse begins slowly or is eased, it could cause interference in a tightly-packed midfield group on a course where Carlisle's undulations can create bunching.

races.name: North Lakes Energy - Harry Doyle Memorial Maiden Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Danrana
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse dropping back to 7f on Good going — her two runs at this trip on Good have produced a 5th and 10th but she has never won or placed in five career starts; Harry Russell faces a big ask from the rear with a saturated hold-up field ahead of him.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Danrana at least has experience of today's distance and going to call on, and 18 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh; the 132 lb burden from stall one is the obvious concern for a filly rated 59 officially.

runners_data.name: Hey Havana
runners_data.note: The only front-runner in the race, Connor Beasley can dictate entirely on her own terms; strong sim-going record (8/10 on similar surfaces) and three places from five starts suggest genuine consistency, though she is technically mapped as Prominent and the STYLE_FIT tag signals she may have been used more patiently in previous races — the solo lead is actually an upgrade in opportunity here.
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in recent starts, Hey Havana has been second three times in his last five outings and has run over today's trip and going, giving him solid grounding heading in; winless of late but his profile makes him the one to beat off 131 lb from stall 7.

runners_data.name: Tago Mago
runners_data.note: Sam England's runner is a genuine hold-up horse whose true rearward position is masked by redistribution in this map — T14 form of 1/7 is encouraging trainer momentum, but Tago Mago's recent string of 6th, 7th and 8th finishes on Good and Standard going over 7-8f suggests finishing kick is limited even when getting a clear run.

runners_data.name: Stoneywell
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a bleak recent record — 7th, 7th, 8th, 9th and 12th in last five — who has failed to place on Good or Good-to-Soft ground; Tom Eaves picks up the ride but the 9-day turnaround and a 138lb burden make it hard to be optimistic from a hold-up berth.
runners_data.comment: Stoneywell has run over today's trip and going before and, rated 63, shapes as a leading danger despite being winless in his last five starts; the main concern is a string of unplaced finishes that will need reversing here.

runners_data.name: Big Apple Jack
runners_data.note: An honest hold-up performer for Michael & David Easterby who has placed four times in 15 runs on similar going, but he arrives just three days after his last outing and is displaced into midfield from his natural rear position — the short turnaround and STYLE_FIT flag both temper expectations.
runners_data.comment: Big Apple Jack shaped with plenty of promise when a second three starts back, and he drops into this off an official mark of just 57 with our rating suggesting more ability than that; the risk is he returns only three days after his last outing.

runners_data.name: Uniter
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's three-year-old has a very poor record over this trip — one placing from nine runs on similar going — and a pulled-up run in recent form is deeply concerning; Sam James takes over but the 19-day break does nothing to mask a lack of form at 7f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Uniter has at least run over today's trip and returns on a quick 19-day turnaround from stall three carrying 133 lb, though a pulled-up effort among recent form makes it hard to build a case at this level.

runners_data.name: Supreme Dancer
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's lightly-raced three-year-old has placed twice in two 7f runs on Good ground (2nd both times), making this trip on this surface his optimum combination; Ethan Tindall claims 5lbs and the 30-day freshener could aid, though his natural hold-up style means he will need a pace to close into — this scenario suits him most when Hey Havana sets an honest gallop.
runners_data.comment: Supreme Dancer has finished second twice in his last five starts and steps back up over a trip and going he has already experienced, making him a strong each-way threat off 130 lb from stall 2; the risk is that he remains winless in recent starts and must find improvement to get his head in front.

runners_data.name: Our Nicola
runners_data.note: 218-day absence is an enormous flag for this four-year-old, who also carries a stamina fade note and has finished 8th, 10th and 11th in three of her last four 7f runs on Standard; David & Nicola Barron have 1/9 T14 form and William Pyle rides — her true hold-up style, pushed into a mapped midfield slot by the crowded field, compounds the difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Our Nicola faces a stiff ask on return from a 218-day absence, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a third five starts back offers a rare crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Agric Ranger
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old has never raced beyond 6f in his career, making this step up to 7f on Good ground an unproven stamina test; the hood (hg:p) suggests some temperament management, and while Oisin McSweeney rides, the combination of a trip question and redistribution from his natural rearward position leaves him needing much to go right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Agric Ranger faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and comes back quickly enough at 12 days since his last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Hey Havana is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she will stride out from the gates and dictate a solo, uncontested pace over Carlisle's 7f on Good ground. The remainder of the field — Danrana, Stoneywell, Uniter and the rest — are hold-up types who will be content to track from midfield to rear, meaning the pace is unlikely to be pressured at any stage and Hey Havana can control the fractions entirely on her own terms. Several runners flagged as true hold-up horses — Tago Mago, Supreme Dancer, Big Apple Jack, Our Nicola and Agric Ranger — are mapped to midfield only because the field is saturated with closers; none of them is likely to challenge Hey Havana for prominent ground, leaving her leadership entirely uncontested. This shape strongly favours a horse with early tactical speed capable of travelling just off the pace in second or third, as the lone leader is rarely truly tested and controlled-pace races over this trip at Carlisle can be won from the front or by the single horse closest to the action.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hey Havana Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hey Havana crosses cleanly, sets a sustainable gallop and is never headed from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: With no rival willing or able to press her, Hey Havana controls every yard at a comfortable tempo, conserving enough energy to repel any late thrust on Good ground — her sim-going record of 8/10 on similar surfaces backs her durability in these conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that the horse in second or third travelling smoothly has a clear momentum advantage turning for home.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop means the horse immediately on Hey Havana's heels gets a perfect tow into the straight and can pounce when the leader ties up; this scenario rewards a prominent-tracking profile with enough quality to quicken past a tired leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Find Gaps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely slow and a bunched field opens up late-race gaps for hold-up horses to thread through.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo paradoxically compresses the field, meaning true hold-up horses carrying lower weights — Agric Ranger (121lbs) and Our Nicola (124lbs) — can benefit if a sprint develops and the leader has nothing left; however, the redistribution of so many closers makes a decisive late sweep unlikely given none are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Implodes — Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If interference, wide draws or a sudden mid-race surge by multiple horses disrupts the anticipated shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Stoneywell's recent poor form and multiple hold-up horses forced into unnatural midfield positions could create erratic pace fluctuations that scramble the order; in a messy finish Danrana, who has hit the frame at 7f on Good, could sneak through.

watchPoints.text: Hey Havana — watch whether Connor Beasley jumps cleanly and establishes the lead immediately; if she misses the break or is crowded early, the entire pace map collapses as there is no backup front-runner.

Supreme Dancer — his two 2nd-place finishes at exactly 7f on Good going mean he is the most likely beneficiary if he can find a position immediately behind Hey Havana; watch where Ethan Tindall places him in the first furlong.

Big Apple Jack — arriving just three days after his last run, watch for any signs of fatigue or reluctance in the pre-race and early stages, as a horse forced into an unnatural midfield position on a short turnaround could cause interference if he hangs or drops away abruptly.
Agric Ranger — making his first career start over 7f, watch his stride pattern in the final two furlongs for signs that the extra distance is stretching him beyond his stamina ceiling.
Our Nicola — the 218-day absence makes her unpredictable early doors; watch for any sluggish or over-keen behaviour coming out of the stalls that could disrupt those drawn alongside her.

races.name: David Allen IT Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Commander Of Life
runners_data.note: Won over course and distance most recently and boasts a 1W4P record in similar going — Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) adds value and a prominent style suits a Lord Capulet-led tempo perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Commander Of Life won last time out and has run over today's distance and going, giving him solid claims, but carrying 133 lb from stall 10 and ranked eighth of twelve on ratings suggests he faces a stiff ask against stronger rivals.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: Headgear-wearing hold-up type whose recent form reads poorly (9th, 6th, 11th) and a noted tendency to fade in the finish is a significant concern in a race where late ground may not materialise; O'Meara's 14-day strike rate of 8/49 offers little comfort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lord Bertie nonetheless rates significantly above his official mark on our figures, and having run over today's distance and going he arrives fit enough on a 26-day break — the talent may finally be about to show.

runners_data.name: Son
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a solid 0W3P record in similar going and a consistent finishing profile, though 12 of 15 recent runs at this trip on Good offer plenty of evidence he rarely wins from off the pace.
runners_data.comment: Son has run over today's trip and going before, and his rating of 86 puts him firmly among the leading dangers off stall four; yet he is winless in his last six starts and that run to fourth three starts back has not been built upon since.

runners_data.name: Native Instinct
runners_data.note: Bethell has a strong 9/23 14-day record and this 4yo won over 7f Good last time, sitting fresh at 50 days off; a hold-up style means he needs gaps to open but the recent form and trainer angle are legitimate positives.
runners_data.comment: Native Instinct won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, with a trainer firing at 39% in the last fortnight, yet 50 days off the track and a busy recent record that includes two sixth-place finishes give reason for caution.

runners_data.name: Hunky Dory
runners_data.note: Prominent-going 4yo carrying headgear on a course and distance that is new territory — all five recent runs have been over 6f on Standard, making this 7f Good assignment a notable unknown; Perratt 14-day 2/12.
runners_data.comment: Hunky Dory arrives in good heart after finishing third last time out, and a winner four starts back, bringing solid recent form into this contest; he has run over today's distance and going, and 135 lb from stall six is the main weight to overcome.

runners_data.name: Misunderstood
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who has been beaten 4th at best in eight recent attempts on Good ground at 6f-7f; the O'Meara yard is active but this horse's form suggests a ceiling that makes him a minor player at best here.
runners_data.comment: Misunderstood has run over today's trip and going and, rated 87 by us against an official mark of 79, looks to have strong claims as the second-ranked runner in the field; the concern is he has been winless in his last six starts, with a best recent finish of fourth.

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Won back-to-back on Standard at 7f and steps onto Good ground for the first time at this trip; the course-and-distance form is therefore uncertain but a prominent style could exploit a steady pace if he handles the surface.
runners_data.comment: King Of Fury has winning form in his last two starts, so fitness and momentum are genuine positives, but ranked ninth of twelve on our figures with a speed rating of 76 well below his rivals, he faces a stiff ask off 134 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Count Palatine
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has been well beaten in both recent 7f Good runs (6th, 14th) but posted a 3rd over 8f Good suggesting some aptitude for this surface; quick 11-day turnaround and a 13/15 run record in similar conditions bears watching.
runners_data.comment: Count Palatine returns quickly on 11 days' rest and has run over today's trip and going, but he is winless in his last five starts, with his most telling recent effort a third three starts back, and a sixth last time out suggests he remains hard to win with.

runners_data.name: Lord Capulet
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with a 1W1P record at 7f Good, winning twice at this trip overall; Kevin Ryan has just 1/22 in the 14-day window but Lord Capulet's tactical position is the key asset — he sets the table for everyone else.
runners_data.comment: Lord Capulet arrives 41 days between runs with his trainer in wretched form at 1/22 over the past fortnight, and his last outing was a sixth, leaving him hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and distance and going; ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, the case for him is thin.

runners_data.name: Havana Prince
runners_data.note: 88 days off is a significant fitness query, and while he has two wins over 7f on Standard, his Good-ground record over this trip reads 14th, 16th — the headgear flag (hg:p) may help but absence and going evidence combine poorly.
runners_data.comment: Havana Prince has winning form in recent starts but arrives on the back of two unplaced efforts and a lengthy 88-day absence, leaving fitness very much in question, and he is ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, making him hard to fancy at this level despite having run over today's distance and going.

runners_data.name: Golden Strike
runners_data.note: Career form shows a 2W2P record in similar going and a recent win over 7f Good, but this natural prominent runner is unlikely to secure that position in today's congested field; the style-fit discount is real and Tindall's 5lb claim only partially offsets it.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back but has since finished seventh and fifth in his last two, so the form has cooled; he has run over today's distance and going before, and 26 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh, though 129 lb is a stern ask for a horse rated 74 officially.

runners_data.name: Vince Lombardi
runners_data.note: 189 days off is a major flag, and while he won over 7f on Standard last time out, his Good-going sample is minimal; like Golden Strike, he is a natural prominent type who figures to be shuffled wider than ideal and Farmer's 5lb claim cannot fully compensate for the absence and the positional squeeze.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures and returning from a 189-day absence, Vince Lombardi has plenty to prove, though he has run over today's distance and going before and his win two starts back offers a crumb of hope.

races.paceDynamic: Lord Capulet is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push him from the gates, he is likely to control a comfortable, measured gallop through the first half of this 7f contest on Good turf at Carlisle. Behind him, Commander Of Life, Hunky Dory, King Of Fury, and Count Palatine all want to race prominently, creating a compressed pack in the early stages that will generate significant traffic trouble between the 2f and 3f markers. Golden Strike and Vince Lombardi are natural prominent horses who are unlikely to find that position in this congested field and have been mapped to midfield as a consequence — the race holds more speed types than can realistically be accommodated at the front. The sustainable, uncontested pace set by Lord Capulet shapes this as a race that will suit horses who can sit just behind the leader with cover and still find a decisive turn of foot in the final furlong — a profile that favours sharp, on-the-pace prominent types who travel smoothly through the traffic rather than deep closers making ground from the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lord Capulet Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Lord Capulet bowls along unchallenged and the prominent pack behind him never fully coalesces into a threat.
scenarios.body: Lord Capulet sets a comfortable tempo, conserves energy through the middle, and his rivals in the prominent group get bottled up in traffic between the 2f-3f pole; he quickens away in the final furlong having never been pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Posse Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion resolves early and one of the chasing pack overtakes Lord Capulet approaching the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Commander Of Life or King Of Fury tracks the leader closely, avoids the worst of the traffic shuffle, and uses the Good ground to reel Lord Capulet in and assert inside the last furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and the race compresses late, allowing a hold-up runner to weave through the tiring bunch.
scenarios.body: Native Instinct or Son, sitting last early, finds a clear run on the rail or outside as the prominent pack folds inside the final furlong; Good ground suits both on historical evidence but they need the gap to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos From Congestion
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent traffic jam produces bumping or checking between 2f-3f out that derails the principals and opens the race wide.
scenarios.body: A horse that avoids the shuffle — possibly Golden Strike or Vince Lombardi, racing out of their natural role in midfield — stumbles into a winning position as the favoured types cancel each other out; their redistribution makes this a low-probability, chaotic outcome.

watchPoints.text: Lord Capulet is the only confirmed front-runner — watch for whether any of the prominent pack (Commander Of Life, King Of Fury, Count Palatine) attempt to challenge him in the first 2f, which would radically alter the pace picture.

The five-horse prominent cluster creates serious traffic risk between 2f and 3f out — any bumping or checking in that group could dramatically alter the result and disadvantage horses like Commander Of Life and Hunky Dory who need a clear passage.

Golden Strike and Vince Lombardi, natural front-rank horses mapped to midfield, should be monitored in the first furlong — if either forces their way forward against the pace shape, it compresses the front further and escalates the congestion risk.

Native Instinct (50 days off) and Havana Prince (88 days off) are both hold-up types returning fresh — watch their early positioning to gauge fitness; either could be caught flat-footed in the first quarter if the pace is stronger than expected.

Lord Bertie's noted tendency to fade in the finish combined with a hold-up style in a race unlikely to produce a strong-pace collapse means he needs to be close enough at the 2f pole to matter — his recent finishes suggest that is unlikely.

races.name: Armstrong Watson Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Maximum Velocity
runners_data.note: Has won and placed repeatedly on Good ground at this trip (sim-going 9 from 12, 1W 4P) and carries hood; Alex Jary's 3lb claim is a genuine asset, and as a natural hold-up runner it needs luck in running in a tight field, though recent 6f form is encouragingly sharp.
runners_data.comment: Maximum Velocity brings fitness on his side after just 12 days off and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but he was fifth last time out and has managed only one win in his last six starts, which is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Yellow Diamonds
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's consistent sort is the lone confirmed pace-setter and will dictate from the front, though its record at this trip is modest (0W 1P from 5 starts at similar going) and there is a hint of vulnerability once headed; the STYLE_FIT flag is irrelevant as it is playing its natural lead role here.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and no stranger to today's trip and going, Yellow Diamonds catches the eye as the top-rated runner in this field, though connections are in a lean spell and she will need to convert that consistency into something more tangible, having been yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Kilmac Air
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello partners a true hold-up performer returning after 77 days off, and the limited similar-going record (1 from 4, 0W 0P) gives little confidence; pushed forward by the volume of closers in this field, it is unlikely to race where it wants and the style displacement is a genuine handicap.
runners_data.comment: Kilmac Air shaped with promise when third two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going gives her a solid platform, with our rating of 71 marking her out as a genuine threat from stall three — though winless in her last four, returning after 77 days is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's runner has placed twice on Good ground at 6f-7f and bounced back just 8 days ago, so freshness is not a concern; a natural hold-up horse that must find a clear passage, and the tight handicap weights mean any position on the rail could prove decisive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Oasis Cover does at least return quickly on eight days' rest and has run over today's trip and going, though a fifth last time out and a second four starts back represent the extent of her recent encouragement, and she faces a stiff task from stall seven off 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Hares Bredth
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's yard has been in solid form (T14: 5 from 84) and David Allan knows the horse well; prominent in style and has won over this C&D trip on Good ground before (1W from 9 sim-going runs), making it the most naturally suited to racing just off Yellow Diamonds and pouncing late.
runners_data.comment: Hares Bredth won three starts back but has posted a sixth and seventh in his two subsequent outings, so his form is patchy at best; he has run over today's trip and going, and 18 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh, though his official mark of 56 leaves little room for error.

runners_data.name: Heathers Feather
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's filly has no win from four career starts and all her form comes on Tapeta or Stanmore, making the Good turf at Carlisle a genuine query; a hold-up type shuffled into the midfield by redistribution, she is racing on an unfamiliar surface in a shape that does not suit.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with finishes no better than fourth in recent outings, Heathers Feather faces a stiff ask from a rating of 43 in an eight-runner field, though 19 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Northern Tempest
runners_data.note: Michael Dods fields a horse with decent Good-ground exposure (4 from 9, 0W 1P) and tongue-tie fitted, but 44 days off and a natural rear-of-field preference that cannot be fulfilled in this compressed field limits its chance; Connor Beasley will have to compromise its position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Northern Tempest nonetheless shaped with promise when fourth and third in recent outings, and has experience of today's trip and conditions; drawn in stall one carrying 124 lb, the main risk is whether he can finally convert that consistency into something more decisive.

runners_data.name: Dream Forever
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a serious concern in a race with a sustainable pace and a large hold-up cohort; Jedd O'Keeffe has not won with this horse in three recent tries, and 90 days off combined with a deeply uninspiring form string (11-12-13 in recent starts) makes it very hard to recommend.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Dream Forever has little obvious appeal here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and at least steps out from stall two fresh after 90 days off.

races.paceDynamic: Yellow Diamonds is the sole confirmed front runner in this 6f handicap at Carlisle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be allowed to dictate a comfortable, controlled tempo from flag to finish. Hares Bredth is the likeliest horse to press from a prominent position, giving Yellow Diamonds something to think about without creating a true contested pace scenario. The remainder of the field — Kilmac Air, Heathers Feather, Northern Tempest, Dream Forever, and Maximum Velocity — are all natural hold-up types, but the volume of closers relative to the size of the field means several will be forced forward from their preferred berth, compressing the midfield rather than hunting a clean run from the rear. With a single front runner setting a sustainable gallop on Good turf over 6f, this race shape strongly favours horses that can race prominently or just off the pace, as the fractions are unlikely to be pressured enough to produce the late gaps that true hold-up performers require. The field contains more genuine rear-of-field types than can realistically settle in those positions — Kilmac Air, Heathers Feather and Northern Tempest are the horses most likely displaced forward against their natural inclination, with none of them certain to secure their preferred pitch.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds dictates an uncontested, even tempo and the closers cannot find daylight through a packed midfield.
scenarios.body: Yellow Diamonds sets fractions it can sustain across 6f on Good ground, and a horse travelling prominently just off the pace inherits the clearest run to the line as the hold-up pack struggles to thread through. This shape is overwhelmingly the most logical outcome given only one confirmed pace horse in a field of eight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds is caught and passed in the closing stages by a horse that travelled just off the pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Hares Bredth or Maximum Velocity, having sat within a length or two of the pace, finds the extra gear in the final furlong as Yellow Diamonds ties up under its weight. Good ground on the Carlisle straight suits a horse with a smooth cruising speed that can sustain its effort from two out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge from Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is stronger than anticipated and the field fans wide, creating a clear lane for a hold-up runner to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: Only in this scenario does a true closer like Kilmac Air or Northern Tempest get to race anywhere near its natural position, and even then the 6f trip and compressed field limits the ground they can make up in the final furlong. The tag-along pace from Yellow Diamonds makes this route the least likely to deliver sufficient gaps at a sprint distance.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Yellow Diamonds sets an unusually slow early pace and the entire field is delivered in a heap entering the final 2f.
scenarios.body: A chaotic finish where any horse with a fresh turn of foot can emerge, but this scenario relies on Yellow Diamonds severely mismanaging the race, which is unlikely under a competent jockey on a horse bred and schooled to lead. Dream Forever's fade tendency and the hold-up horses' displacement make this a low-value, scattershot outcome.

watchPoints.text: Yellow Diamonds holds an enormous tactical advantage as the sole front runner — watch whether Ryan Sexton takes control immediately from the gates or allows any other runner to press and disrupt the framing of this race.

Kilmac Air, Heathers Feather and Northern Tempest are all genuine hold-up types who cannot all settle where they want — watch for early jostling and shuffling in the first two furlongs as riders negotiate for position.

Hares Bredth's Good-ground record at this trip is the strongest in the field among the prominent types — watch whether David Allan positions it prominently enough behind Yellow Diamonds to exploit a sustainable pace rather than getting swamped by the hold-up runners bunching ahead of it.

Dream Forever's fade tendency and 90-day absence make it a significant drifter to monitor in the market — if it shortens, it may signal track or ground information; if it lengthens significantly, treat its chances as negligible in this shape.

Maximum Velocity's hood and Alex Jary's 3lb claim are both worth tracking — the claim in particular reduces the weight burden in a tight 6f handicap, and a fast-jumping start that gets it into a better position than its natural hold-up style would suggest could make it a factor.

races.name: Knights Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Avatar Jet
runners_data.note: Has won over this exact trip on Good-to-Soft/Standard ground and was placed twice at the same course and distance, giving confidence over the track — a genuine hold-up performer who will need Between Me And U to have gone quick enough to close into, and Zak Wheatley must judge his run perfectly from the back.
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back and a winner four starts back, Avatar Jet brings distance and going experience to this, and 27 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; however, a seventh last time out and a mark of 66 hint at inconsistency that makes him a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Hostility
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's yard is firing at 8/49 over 14 days which is modest, but Hostility has won twice over eight furlongs on Good recently and Conor Whiteley (5) can claim; sits naturally in a prominent position and is extremely well-suited if this race runs to a standard tempo with no serious pace pressure.
runners_data.comment: Hostility advertises rock-solid recent form with a win last time out and another victory three starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and going, so conditions hold no fears; the fifth two starts back is the one blot to keep onside.

runners_data.name: Ephron
runners_data.note: A 3yo whose two victories have both come over eight furlongs on Good going — directly applicable form — and Connor Beasley is a strong booking; natural hold-up performer who needs a strong enough gallop to bring his finish into play, and the step back from 9-10f trips looks like a positive.
runners_data.comment: Ephron won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, arriving here in good nick just 18 days on; carrying a hefty 136 lb from stall 10 is the chief question he must answer.

runners_data.name: Ravishing Beauty
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe's charge has headgear (visor) and a solid placed record on Good over this trip, with two wins on Soft suggesting the ground is fine; in reality a prominent racer who will struggle to get that position with Between Me And U and Keep An Eye On It ahead, meaning she races slightly outside her comfort zone today.
runners_data.comment: Ravishing Beauty has run over today's trip and going, and a win four starts back hints at ability, though consecutive third-placed finishes have given way to a fourth last time out, suggesting she finds winning elusive; 136 lb from stall four makes the task no easier.

runners_data.name: Between Me And U
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's 5yo wears a tongue-tie and has won twice on Standard (all-weather) over this trip, but his three Good-ground runs produced 7th, 6th and 6th — the going switch is a legitimate concern; nevertheless he is the lone confirmed front-runner and David Allan should find himself with an uncontested lead regardless of his finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins make Between Me And U one to respect, though finishes of sixth, sixth and seventh before that show he can disappoint; has run over today's trip and going before, and 142 lb from stall six is the key question on whether that winning streak can continue.

runners_data.name: Barley
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 7yo has an enviable placed record — seven placings in his last five runs at this trip, all on Good — and was out just 4 days ago suggesting the stable is happy; a genuine hold-up type whose consistency is admirable but who has not won over this trip and may again fill a place rather than take the spoils.
runners_data.comment: Barley has placed in five of his last six starts, most recently second two runs back and third three runs back, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the main concern is a tendency to find one too good, leaving him yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Keep An Eye On It
runners_data.note: Tony Coyle and Kaine Wood's 3yo is stepping up sharply from 7f after winning over a mile on Soft and placing at 7f on Good — David Nolan is a strong claiming booking — and the natural prominent style means he could push across into second early, making him a key player if the tempo is honest.

runners_data.name: Blufferonthebus
runners_data.note: Craig Lidster's 5yo returns from a 47-day break which is a notable freshness flag, and his recent form includes a placed effort on Soft over this trip; a true hold-up runner whose instinct is to come from well off the pace, but with the field compressed he may find himself not as far back as he would like, meaning his finishing effort could arrive earlier than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked ninth of eleven on our figures, Blufferonthebus faces a stiff ask here, though she does bring distance and going experience and her third last time out shows she retains some ability.

runners_data.name: Beckon
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's 3yo has been prominent or chasing the pace in recent starts but recent form tailed off (9th last time on Soft over 8f) and the trainer has a 0/4 record over 14 days; a front-of-midfield type who may box-seat a prominent position and suits if the race is run at a fair pace, though consistency is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Ninth last time out makes Beckon hard to fancy, and she ranks tenth of eleven on our figures, but she has run over today's trip before and a win in her last five starts shows she can find the track.

runners_data.name: Princess Niyla
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's 6yo is a regular Good-ground performer with 12 of 15 applicable runs on that surface, wears headgear (hood), and Paul Mulrennan is an able pilot; her instinct is to race held up from the rear, but the field shape means she will likely sit closer to midfield than she ideally wants, softening the effect of her usual late kick.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last six starts, Princess Niyla was a solid third two runs back but slipped to seventh last time out just seven days ago, suggesting the quick turnaround is a query; she has run over today's trip and going, though her 132 lb burden won't help.

runners_data.name: Captain Corelli
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's 9yo returns from a massive 272-day absence — the single biggest flag in this race — and his last five runs over this trip on Good produced a string of mid-to-rear finishes; a natural hold-up runner who will be further forward than usual due to field redistribution, and the layoff combined with age makes him very hard to support.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning from a 272-day absence, Captain Corelli faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures, and his trainer's current 5% strike rate offers little encouragement; experience over today's trip and going is about all he has in his favour.

races.paceDynamic: Between Me And U is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to push them into a contested gallop, David Allan should be able to dictate a controlled, honest pace from the front over this flat Carlisle mile on Good ground. Ravishing Beauty, Blufferonthebus, Princess Niyla and Captain Corelli are all natural prominent or hold-up types who have been redistributed on the map because the field contains more pace-hungry runners than can realistically secure their preferred berth — Between Me And U and Keep An Eye On It are most likely to pin down the early positions, with Hostility and Beckon pressing close behind. That settled, single-pace scenario over a flat track on Good ground historically rewards horses who travel prominently in behind the leader and have the tactical speed to kick when the tempo stays honest — closers with a genuine sustained finish, like Avatar Jet, Ephron and Barley, remain dangerous but need the pace to lift sufficiently in the straight to bring their late runs into play. The tactical verdict is clear: a lone front-runner setting a moderate, uncontested gallop on Good ground at Carlisle favours prominent racers who can sit second or third and pounce in the home straight, with true hold-up horses disadvantaged by the likely lack of a strong finishing surge to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Between Me And U dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is decided by those tracking closely in the first two or three positions.
scenarios.body: Between Me And U sets fractions entirely on their own terms and the race resolves in the straight as horses positioned just off the leader's back quicken past; with no pace pressure there is no dramatic late fanning-out of closers to worry about.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Keep An Eye On It or Hostility push up to sit close to Between Me And U throughout, creating a genuine two-way battle that produces a faster overall tempo.
scenarios.body: A more pressured gallop stretches the field earlier and brings the strongest stayers in the prominent group to the fore in the final two furlongs; Hostility's recent course-and-distance win at Good and Keep An Eye On It's stepping-up trip profile both suit this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Mow Them Down
scenarios.trigger: If the front end runs genuinely fast enough — against expectations — to set up a strong late surge from the back half of the field.
scenarios.body: Avatar Jet and Ephron, both genuine hold-up types with course-appropriate form on Good ground, need the pace to be honest enough to create a gap at the death; Ephron's two wins over eight furlongs on Good are directly relevant here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If Between Me And U fails to fire or checks early, eliminating the only genuine pace influence and causing the field to bunch without a coherent gallop.
scenarios.body: A messy, slow-run race with no settled pace benefits horses who are naturally adaptable and can quicken from a compact mid-pack group; this is the lowest-probability shape because the redistribution means many supposed closers are not true hold-up types.

watchPoints.text: Between Me And U's Good-ground record (three runs, no wins or places) is a direct concern — if David Allan cannot maintain a clean lead or begins to weaken turning in, the entire pace scenario collapses and the race becomes chaotic.

Keep An Eye On It is stepping up sharply in trip from 7f and could press Between Me And U aggressively early — if he tests the front-runner before the straight, the resulting pace increase could bring the true closers Avatar Jet and Ephron into the picture far more than Scenario A would suggest.

Barley's four-day turnaround is unusually short for Tim Easterby's yard — watch the market move to gauge whether the trainer intends a bold showing or is simply giving the horse a run; consistent placed form at this trip makes him dangerous if fresh.

Hostility's recent five-run form string (1-2-1-5-7) alternates sharply — the two wins were on Good over 8f matching today's conditions exactly, but the two moderate performances were on Good at 9f; the step back to a mile looks the right call and is worth noting as a positive angle.

Captain Corelli's 272-day absence and age (9) make him one to watch in the paddock for condition — if he looks fresh and well he remains a historical performer on Good over this trip, but on paper the layoff alone makes him an outsider in any scenario.
